newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris urges caution in Congo as some French flee.
newsitem.headline: Paris urges caution in Congo as some French flee.

text.p: Paris urged French residents of Congo Brazzaville to remain in their homes on Sunday following the overnight shooting death of a French soldier in the capital Brazzaville.

An Air France plane carrying 78 people fleeing Brazzaville, most of them French citizens, arrived in Paris overnight, and those on board told of harrowing incidents of looting and violence as well as widespread anti-French sentiment in the former French colony.

"We did not want to leave, as we did not want to lose everything, but it became necessary. We were threatened with knives and machetes because we were French," one man told France Info radio on landing in Paris.
Some of those on board had come to the airport with nothing but the clothes on their back. One man arrived even without shoes, according to witnesses.

Four days of clashes pitting supporters of former president Denis Sassou Nguesso against soldiers loyal to President Pascal Lissouba and other political and ethnic rivals have rocked the capital Brazzaville.
Nguesso told Radio France Internationale on Sunday that he would be prepared to end the fighting if Lissouba "admits that he is the aggressor," among other conditions.
Nguesso said Lissouba also must "cease bombardments of the northern parts of the city and stop slaughtering opposition leaders".
Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said the estimated 2,200 French citizens in the Brazzaville area should remain in their homes and keep in close contact with the French embassy.
"We are closely watching the situation," he said. But France was not calling at this time for its citizens to leave.

The U.S. State Department strongly urged American citizens to leave the Congo on Saturday, and a group of 44 Americans flew out of Brazzaville for Kinshasa, the capital of Laurent Kabila's neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo.

Doutriaux said some 100 French residents of Brazzaville had been taken from their homes on Saturday and regrouped in safe areas due to anti-French sentiment and outbreaks of unspecified "deplorable incidents" in the capital.
A French soldier was killed and five others wounded in the course of one such rescue mission involving both French and Congolese soldiers, the French Defence Ministry said.
A senior officer in the Congolese army was also hurt in the clash, a ministry spokesman said.
A ministry statement said the confrontation was triggered when a group of foreign residents including some French citizens found themselves pinned down in a building and requested help.
"With the approval of the Congolese authorities, Congolese and French troops present in Brazzaville proceeded at the demand of the foreign citizens to help them get away," the statement said.
"As a second wave of evacuations began, some of the French and Congolese troops came under fire from uncontrolled elements," the statement said.
The incident occurred between 1900 and 2000 GMT on Saturday evening, the statement said.
Doutriaux said there were about 450 French soldiers in Brazzaville.

They came to the capital several months ago and like U.S, British, Belgian and Portuguese troops remained on standby to evacuate foreign nationals from Kinshasa in the event of a bloodbath there during the final days of the civil war that brought Kabila to power. The others all left.
